title: Syhiba in Wakefield Earns 4.8 Stars for Authentic Punjabi and Indian Food
excerpt: The Halifax-born restaurant group, in Wakefield since 2017, pairs chef specialities like shahi korma with an £18.95 early bird menu — and 1,085 Tripadvisor reviewers rate it 4.8 out of 5.
body:
• Syhiba in Wakefield, West Yorkshire, holds a 4.8 out of 5 rating on Tripadvisor from 1,085 reviews, according to the Bradford Telegraph and Argus — the latest local spotlight on the family restaurant group.
  • The restaurant serves Punjabi, Pakistani and Indian dishes at 17 George Street, Wakefield WF1 1NE; it first opened in Halifax in 1996 and added the Wakefield restaurant in 2017.
  • Its early bird menu runs Sunday to Thursday, 5pm to 8pm, at £18.95 per person for poppadoms and a pickle tray, a starter, any main dish and any sundry — order by 8pm, and the deal is cash only.
  • Chef specialities named on the menu include shahi korma, chicken tikka makhani and balti seekh kebab, alongside bhuna, madras and dopiaza curries and a wide vegetarian selection.

Bradford is often called the curry capital of Britain, but a short trip east to Wakefield leads to one of West Yorkshire's highest-rated curry houses. Syhiba, on George Street in Wakefield city centre, has been singled out by the Bradford Telegraph and Argus for what it calls an amazing selection of authentic Punjabi, Pakistani and Indian food — backed by a 4.8 out of 5 rating on Tripadvisor from 1,085 reviewers.

A Halifax original that expanded

Syhiba first opened in Halifax in 1996. The Wakefield restaurant followed in 2017, giving the group two Yorkshire locations. On its own website, the restaurant says it specialises in authentic Punjabi, Pakistani and Indian cuisine made from traditional ingredients, and describes itself as one of the best loved and most popular restaurants in West Yorkshire. The Wakefield site is at 17 George Street, WF1 1NE, behind the Morrisons store, on the site of the old Lalas restaurant.

What is on the menu

The menu mixes starters such as samosas, kebabs and pakora — including a mixed starter for sharing — with chef specialities that include shahi korma, chicken tikka makhani and balti seekh kebab. Familiar favourites run from bhuna and madras curries to baltis and dopiaza, with grill dishes, a wide range of vegetarian options, and the usual spread of rices and naans. Google's listing for the restaurant shows evening opening: from 5pm Tuesday to Saturday, and from 4pm on Sundays.

The early bird is the value play

The deal most reviewers mention is the early bird menu: Sunday to Thursday, 5pm to 8pm, £18.95 per person covers poppadoms with a pickle tray, a starter of your choice, any main dish and any sundry. The restaurant's site adds the conditions — you must order by 8pm to qualify, the whole table must take the deal, and it is cash only. One returning Tripadvisor reviewer quoted by the Telegraph and Argus described being recognised and seated by a staff member, Ash, two years after their last visit, and rated his recommendations 10 out of 10; another called it an exceptional visit to their favourite restaurant, praising food served piping hot and polite, professional staff.

Planning a visit

Syhiba takes bookings through its website or by phone on 01924 298929, and reviewers advise booking ahead — the early bird sittings in particular fill up. For diaspora readers in Leeds, Bradford and the wider West Yorkshire area, it is a well-evidenced alternative to the usual Bradford curry run: three decades in business, a second city conquered, and a rating most restaurants never reach.
